proposal.topic: Day-1 Production Release Value Strategy: Prioritizing High-Utility In-Memory Computational Engines
proposal.description: To maximize the practical, tangible utility of TRM Swarm OS on Day 1 of public/production release, the Council must deliberate and ratify the implementation priority for the remaining virtual SRAM architectures. Rather than abstract or unfalsifiable constructs, the platform requires industry-standard computational primitives that deliver immediate benchmarkable performance: 1) Systolic Array Engine: In-memory parallel 2D GEMM (General Matrix Multiply) acceleration for ML/neural inference; 2) Sparse Attention Engine: Block-sparse attention mask evaluation for Transformer token context windows; 3) Graph Neural Network (GNN) Engine: Relational graph message-passing and node feature aggregation; 4) Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM): Energy-based unsupervised feature extraction via Contrastive Divergence. The Council will deliberate on which engines create the highest immediate day-1 enterprise and developer value, ratify the deployment sequence, and bind the execution through the K3 Ternary Logic and TurboVec pipeline.

prioritized_roadmap.name: Systolic Array (2D GEMM)
prioritized_roadmap.rationale: Direct linear algebra acceleration for neural network inference and matrix math; highest immediate day-1 utility across all developer workflows.

prioritized_roadmap.name: Sparse Attention Engine
prioritized_roadmap.rationale: Essential primitive for efficient transformer context processing and KV-cache compression; high demand in LLM deployment.

prioritized_roadmap.name: Graph Neural Network (GNN)
prioritized_roadmap.rationale: Enables relational knowledge graph reasoning, agent mesh topology analysis, and molecular graph evaluation.

prioritized_roadmap.name: Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM)
prioritized_roadmap.rationale: Energy-based generative modeling and unsupervised feature extraction complementing the Hopfield energy framework.
